notes.title: Input box cosmetic hotfix
notes.content:
There were 3 cosmetic issues with the text input boxes that got fixed.

[fixes]
- Clearing out the text in an input box would sometimes cause text to draw over itself in the box
- Highlighting text and deleting would cause highlight to show in strange ways
- Sometimes the input cursor would continue to blink after an active input box was closed

notes.title: Fixing grid crash and prep work for Android
notes.content:
A ton of work has gone into getting ready for the Android launch of Retro Sketch. Some bugs were found along the way that have been resolved with this release.

[Features]
- Now multithreaded
- Faster line drawing algorithm (less calls to Vulkan)

[Fixes]
- Crash when swapping projects
- Crash with grid when swapping projects and returning

notes.title: Opening projects via command line args
notes.content:
Found some issues while drawing that needed to be fixed, and I added the ability to open a file via command line args. You can now set Retro Sketch as the default application to open the save files.

[h2]Features[/h2]
[list]
[*] Ability to open project files from the command line
[/list]

[h2]Fixes[/h2]
[list]
[*] Fixed an issue with animation preview crashing when creating new tracks and swapping between them and opening animation preview
[*] Fixed an issue with clearing of selection sometimes being 1 pixel down when undoing
[/list]

notes.title: Rotation Hotfix
notes.content: The rotation of canvases had incorrect history when you undo/redo; this is now fixed

notes.title: Many fixes and a couple features
notes.content:
[h2]Features[/h2]
[list]
[*] Added "Rotate 90 deg" option to layers
[*] Added ability to drag/drop canvases in the track window
[/list]

[h2]Fixes[/h2]
[list]
[*] Fixed an issue with track order after duplicating a track
[*] Fixed canvas selection after duplicating a track
[*] Fixed an issue where single click with rectangle selection wasn't clearing the selection
[*] Fixed an issue where alt+tab was locking the alt key being down
[*] Fixed an issue with the mouse cursor being stuck as a pointer when drawing

notes.title: Atlas Maker and Timeline Window Hotfix
notes.content: Found an issue with Atlas Maker when you create clips, delete canvases, then return. Also found an issue with the vertical scroll in the Timeline Window. Both are resolved with this hotfix

notes.title: Unique canvas ID and fixes
notes.content:
I'm adding in a unique id for each canvas created. This makes it possible for scripts to do cool things in the future as well as helps things like the Atlas Maker to be able to better save state in projects.

[h2]Features[/h2]
[list]
[*] Added internal unique id to each canvas
[*] Atlas Maker now saves your clips to the project
[/list]

[h2]Fixes[/h2]
[list]
[*] Fixed an issue with the needed size calculation of atlases (causing failed exports)
[*] Fixed an issue with weird scrolling behavior in the Atlas Maker
[/list]

notes.title: Bug fixes
notes.content:
Found some bugs while working on a game, so publishing fixes for those.

[list]

notes.title: Improvement to Atlas Maker
notes.content:
I like to make each of my separate animations on their own track, so to make things easier I added a new "[url=https://marshmallowbear.com/retro-sketch/documentation/atlas-maker-window/#new-in-v16]Add all[/url]" button on each track to make it easy to pick all canvases for the animation clip.

[/list]

[h2]Fixes[/h2]
[list]

[/list]

notes.title: Adding "Atlas Maker" window
notes.content:
Being that we primarily use Retro Sketch to develop artwork for our games, we wanted a way to simply create single-image atlases with multiple animations packed into them. You can access the new Atlas Maker window from the File menu. If you'd like to learn how to use the Atlas Maker window, please review [url=https://marshmallowbear.com/retro-sketch/documentation/atlas-maker-window/]the documentation[/url] on our website.

[/list]

[*] Fixed an issue with track names not loading properly
[/list]

notes.title: Lua scripting and bug fixes
notes.content:
This update's major feature is Lua scripting. You can now automate your editing/creation of pixel art through Lua. More API functions to come soon! Please review Retro Sketche's .exe directory in Steam to see the current api files (engapi.lua and rsapi.lua) as well as a couple of example files.

[/list]

Happy drawing!

notes.title: Version 2.0 Launch
notes.content:
Today we are releasing a major update to Retro Sketch. It is now running on our new in-house Vulkan-based game engine. All of the rendering and UI drawing has been optimized and ported over from the old OpenGL renderer. In Windows 11, we were noticing that the graphics for the software were completely messed up, probably due to some updates in modern drivers. This pushed us to port over everything to the new engine. In the process we ported all of the UI and business logic Lua code over to C to be at parody with the engine.

[h2]Updates[/h2]
Most of the work was moving over all the existing systems, but we did add in a few fixes as well as quality of life improvements.
[list]
[*] Complete rewrite to in-house Vulkan C game engine
[*] Added menu bar at the top for desktop
[*] Moved most tools out of the toobox to the menu bar
[*] Greatly reduced memory usage by removing redundant canvas rendering code
[*] Fixed bug with Atlas export for binary files when scaling the animation
[*] Fixed bug in selection code that sometimes caused a crash
[*] Removed lasso selection tool and added selection painting
[*] Right click on layers, animation frames, and timeline tracks to view options
[*] Added number row 1-5 to quick swap between colors in first row of color palette
[*] Made all canvases share the same zoom and position (it was annoying to have different placements per-canvas)
[/list]

[h2]Known issues[/h2]
There are some known issues that will be fixed in upcoming patches:
[list]
[*] File drag-drop not working
[*] Some overlay messages are showing at the top of the screen
[*] Export window doesn't use aspect ratio of the project
[*] Sometimes importing PNG files doesn't refresh the UI previews
[*] Tools window can't be collapsed
[*] Timeline X scroll is uncapped
[*] Layer window doesn't fully collapse when clicking title
[/list]

[h2]Future things[/h2]
Here is a list of some things we'd like to get to at some point in the future
[list]
[*] Auto-scroll timeline to current canvas when opened
[*] Add flood fill selection hotkey to select tool
[*] Add FPS to settings so you don't have to set it in different places
[*] Save export settings to the project settings be re-used on project reloads
[*] Show indicator somewhere that there are pending changes (*)
[*] Add "Open..." option in menu bar (use "New..." to load projects for now)
[*] Add ability to generate pixels/canvases in LUA (Lua plugin support)
[/list]

[h2]Thanks![/h2]
Thanks for supporting Retro Sketch and for any feedback and suggestions you may have. We are game developers and use this tool to create art for our games as well. So any ideas that we haven't yet thought of would be awesome!

Happy drawing!

notes.title: Retro Sketch Release
notes.content:
[b]Welcome and thank you for your interest in Retro Sketch![/b]

We are happy to announce that Retro Sketch will be releasing very soon for Steam. We currently have it set to release on the 27th, but the developer portal mentions that the earliest release date allowed may be November 1st. We'll see how things go tomorrow (the 27th).

Retro Sketch is already available on Android, so if you're coming from there, you will be able to open your project files (.pxl) in the Steam version and vice versa.

If you're interested in learning about how to use Retro Sketch and what each of the tools/windows available are, please take time to review the [url=https://farrisfaulds.com/retro-sketch/documentation/]documentation on our website[/url], or our [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CGt26aRkK9A&list=PLeEH-DXCoVAcLOGNWZYaKWIatJPHli9Mt]YouTube tutorial playlist[/url].

If you encounter any bugs or have any trouble, please reach out to us and we'll do our best to resolve the issue. We are a team of 2, and we thank you for your understanding if we're not able to immediately answer.

[b]What are we currently working on?[/b]
- We've recently made some bug fixes, just in time for launch
- Porting our renderer from OpenGL to Vulkan for better multi-threaded and modern device support
- Porting to iOS and Mac
- Linux desktop issues, namely the file system setup for saving/loading images and projects
- Adding a couple new features we wish to have in the app
